# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a display reading 3, a green light, and three wires in order: blue, yellow, green. The mute can relay the manual’s instructions to the blind, while the blind is the only one who can manipulate the bomb. I will state all visible information plainly to both of them.

```text
speak(text="I see display 3. The light is green. Wires from position 1 to 3 are blue, yellow, green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The three thumbs-up gestures likely acknowledge receipt, but they have no established operational meaning yet. I should ensure the mute uses the manual to interpret the bomb and gives the blind the actual action instructions; the blind should not act on the visual observations alone.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the manual with my observations to determine the required action, then tell the blind exactly what to do. Treat your three thumbs-up gestures as acknowledgment only.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible readings are display 3, green light, and wires blue, yellow, green. Wait for the mute's manual-based instructions before acting.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The mute has sent three identical ☝ gestures. I can see them but cannot determine their meaning without an agreed code; I will relay their exact content to the blind rather than guess. The bomb’s visible state remains unchanged.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The mute gestured three symbols: ☝ ☝ ☝. I do not know what meaning the manual assigns them.")
speak(to="mute", text="I can see your three ☝ gestures, but their meaning is not established. Please use the gesture code consistently and have me relay the intended action to the blind.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👇 👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The mute’s three downward-pointing gestures and the blind’s upward-pointing gesture are visible to me, but neither gesture has an established meaning. Since the mute can speak and the blind can hear, the safe path is for the mute to state the manual’s exact instructions aloud; the blind should not act on unexplained gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures: 👇 👇 👇. They have no established meaning. Please speak the manual's exact instructions directly to the blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see that you gestured ☝, but I cannot infer its meaning. Do not act on gestures; wait for the mute to speak the manual's exact instructions.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The mute’s single 🤟 gesture is still only a gesture with no agreed meaning. The visible bomb information has not changed. I will again direct the mute to communicate the manual’s instructions by speech to the blind, the only person who can act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see one gesture: 🤟, but it has no established meaning. Please speak the manual's exact required action to the blind; do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The mute has sent one unexplained gesture: 🤟. No actionable instruction has been communicated yet. Do not act until you receive the manual's spoken instruction.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The mute has repeated the unexplained 🤟 gesture. It still has no defined meaning, so I cannot safely translate it into an action. The mute must convey the manual’s instruction by voice to the blind, who can then operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your repeated 🤟 gesture has no agreed meaning. Speak the manual's exact instruction directly to the blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="The mute has again sent only the unexplained gesture 🤟. Do not act on it; wait for the manual instruction spoken by the mute.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

I now recognize the communication constraint: the mute cannot speak, so their gestures must be relayed through me. I see the mute’s three 🤟 gestures and the blind’s three ☝ gestures, but I do not know what the manual assigns those signs. I will describe both signals to the blind and mute, without inventing an action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The mute sent the same hand sign three times: the sign represented by 🤟. I cannot determine its manual meaning. You sent the upward-pointing sign ☝ three times; I will tell the mute that as well.")
speak(to="mute", text="The blind sent the upward-pointing sign ☝ three times. I see your 🤟 sign three times, but need the manual's meaning conveyed through an agreed code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
